title: Microscopy Lab Student Workforce Development: The University of Utah, Electron Microscopy Lab’s Approach on Transforming Undergraduate Student Aides from Lab Technicians to Professional Analysts
content: The transition from a technician to an analyst represents a critical developmental stage in a student's professional journey, requiring a shift from procedural task execution to analytical problem-solving and decision-making. Unfortunately, such a transition is something that most undergraduate lab technicians do not experience. Undergraduate lab technicians usually have limited work responsibilities. They typically include routine tasks such as lab maintenance, operating a microscope or some other instrument, collecting data and assisting other instrument users. Most labs confine their lab aides to these responsibilities expecting nothing more. The “learning opportunity” part of the job offer is contingent to the availability of the supervisor and their willingness to teach or train the undergraduate lab aide on something beyond what the work requires.
